To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reduction of copper-zinc oxides is much slower than the reduction of pure CuO or CuO-Zn O, and that the presence of ZnO hinders the nucleation and growth of metallic copper particles.

the presence of Al2O3 in the CuO|Zno|Al2O 3=60| 30|10 catalyst, obtained from a precursor prepared by coprecipitation, hinders the reduction of CuO to Cu and the formation of metallic copper particles.
the reduction process of copper–zinc–aluminum oxide methanol catalysts proceeds through the formation, in the intermediate stages, of Cu2O and metallic copper particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the preparation and the reduction process of a methanol synthesis catalyst, based on copper, zinc oxide and alumina, which has been obtained by the thermal decomposition of the corresponding hydroxycarbonates.
the reduction process of copper oxide (Cu2O) to metallic copper (Cu) on the CuO-Zn0 catalysts used for methanol synthesis.
the reduction of CuO-Zn(Al)2O3 catalyst precursors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of alumina has a detrimental effect on the reduction of Cu2+ species to Cuo or Cu+ and on the formation of Cu2O.
the presence of ZnO, CuO and Al2O3, in a three component catalyst, hinders the reduction of the copper species and the formation of the metallic copper.
the presence of alumina, in the form of a hydroxycarbonate precursor, hinders the reduction of the catalysts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reduction of CuO-Zn(Al)2O3 catalyst to metallic Cu is a slow process which involves the reduction of Cu2+ to Cu+ and Cu+ to Cu0.

the presence of alumina (or zinc) in intimate contact with copper oxide (or zinc oxide) in the catalyst precursor, inhibits the nucleation and growth of copper oxide (or of zinc oxide) particles during the reduction process, and that the reduction of Cu2+ species is also inhibited.
the reduction of CuO to Cu2O is not a simple process, and that the reduction of both the copper and zinc oxides in the CuO-Zn0 system is hindered by the presence of alumina.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reduction process of the CuO-Zn0-Al2O3 methanol catalysts is very slow, and that this slow reduction is related to the intimate contact between alumina and CuO and/or ZnO.
the reduction process of CuO is strongly influenced by the presence of ZnO and Al2O3.
the preparation of CuO-ZnAl2O3 catalyst by the decomposition of hydroxcarbonate precursors at 300°C in air leads to a catalyst which is not reducible at temperatures below 400°C.
